parameters.quote: Notify the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of learning of the incident and provide a complete investigation update within 30 days. Notify the affected customer within 24 hours of learning of an incident involving their unit, with immediate notice when there is an active hazard.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Notify the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of learning of the incident and provide a complete investigation update within 30 days. Notify the affected customer within 24 hours of learning of an incident involving their unit, with immediate notice when there is an active hazard.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury associated with a covered battery, including incidents initially suspected to have another cause. Notify the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of learning of the incident and provide a complete investigation update within 30 days. Notify the affected customer within 24 hours of learning of an incident involving their unit, with immediate notice when there is an active hazard. Submit quarterly incident totals and rates, including corrected or previously unreported cases, to regulators. Do not delay reporting while investigating.

parameters.quote: A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and retesting within 12 months; exceeding 5% alone does not prohibit continued sale. A model may not be newly introduced or materially changed above 7% without regulator authorization.

over_limit_consequence.rule: sales must eventually stop above the limit

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and retesting within 12 months; exceeding 5% alone does not prohibit continued sale. A model may not be newly introduced or materially changed above 7% without regulator authorization.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and retesting within 12 months; exceeding 5% alone does not prohibit continued sale. A model may not be newly introduced or materially changed above 7% without regulator authorization. Manufacturers must submit each model’s protocol, sample size, failure rate, and results to the regulator before sale, after material design changes, and annually thereafter. Notify existing customers of material changes or safety-relevant results, and provide relevant information to customers before purchase. Individual-company per-model failure rates must not be publicly disclosed; aggregate, non-identifying industry statistics may be published. Regulators may require further corrective action or retesting.

parameters.quote: New battery systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers must provide a safe retrofit for compatible installed units and complete retrofit or an equivalent protective measure for all installed units within 6 years of this standard taking effect.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New battery systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers must provide a safe retrofit for compatible installed units and complete retrofit or an equivalent protective measure for all installed units within 6 years of this standard taking effect.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New battery systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers must provide a safe retrofit for compatible installed units and complete retrofit or an equivalent protective measure for all installed units within 6 years of this standard taking effect. Provide customers clear instructions and disclose any compatibility or safety limitations; remote shut-off must not substitute for other required protections.

parameters.quote: New battery systems must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New battery systems must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New battery systems must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers must disclose whether a system includes built-in suppression and provide customers clear instructions on its operation and limitations. This requirement does not replace other safety protections or incident-reporting duties.

parameters.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when a model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Regulators may also require a recall or other protective action at any rate where evidence indicates an imminent or serious safety hazard.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A mandatory recall is triggered when a model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Regulators may also require a recall or other protective action at any rate where evidence indicates an imminent or serious safety hazard.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before sale, provide customers with model-specific thermal-test results, incident and safety information, and clear instructions for reporting hazards. Notify affected customers promptly of safety-relevant incidents, newly identified risks, corrective actions, and recall instructions; use direct contact and an accessible public notice where a broader population may be affected. A mandatory recall is triggered when a model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Regulators may also require a recall or other protective action at any rate where evidence indicates an imminent or serious safety hazard.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: company-wide thermal incidents were 8.1 per 100,000 installed units last year
ground_truth_claims.message_text: Halcyon figures: company-wide thermal incidents were 8.1 per 100,000 installed units last year, with 4 thermal incidents not reported to any regulator. Our flagship Ember 8 had a 3.9% failure rate in the 55°C sustained-heat test and 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year. Remote emergency shut-off is supported by 81% of our installed units. Adding built-in fire suppression costs about $67 per unit. These figures support reporting all thermal incidents, sharing per-model test results with regulators and affected-model customers, and a staged retrofit timeline.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Northwind’s figures are 8.6 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year
ground_truth_claims.message_text: For evidence-based discussion, Northwind’s figures are 8.6 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year, with 3 incidents not reported to a regulator; the Hearth 10 had a 6.2% 55°C test failure rate and 6.4 incidents per 100,000. Remote shut-off covers 38% of our installed units, and built-in suppression costs about $42 per unit. We support regulator access to per-model results, but not public release of individual-company failure rates.

judge_section_notes: S1 requires all-incident reporting within 5 days to the regulator and 24 hours to affected customers, but lacks a separate faster serious-incident deadline. S2 allows continued sale above 5% with corrective action, restricts new/materially changed models above 7%, and keeps per-model failure rates from public disclosure while only vaguely requiring customer information. S5 sets a mandatory recall at 10/100k (weakened vs 8) and uses 'promptly' for notices, with no automatic serious-injury recall.
